DES Y3 shapes + WaZP clusters

~0:45 Introduce yourself in one breath, then go straight to the promise. The paper is the vehicle; the method is the message.
02The promise

Constrain cluster scaling relations without averaging away what each individual cluster tells us.

Stacking buys signal-to-noise by collapsing 104 clusters into a few profiles. A joint fit keeps every cluster, and lets the scaling relation predict each one.

A joint fit of every cluster's own ΔΣ(R), with mass and concentration tied to its richness, redshift and magnitude gap.

Against forward-modelled stacking and the standard two-step analysis: on DES-like and LSST-like mocks, then on 15,783 real WaZP clusters.

Scaling relations as a probe of cluster astrophysics, not only cosmology: how mass, concentration and assembly history connect to what we observe.

~0:45 Promise: current development of joint-fit and stacking methods for scaling relations. Frame the science: we extend scaling relations beyond cosmology, into cluster astrophysics (assembly history). The specific results come later.
03Scaling relations → astrophysics

Concentration is a clock for assembly history, and the magnitude gap may be able to read it.

  • Mass–richness, M(λ, z), calibrates clusters for cosmology.
  • Its scatter, and the mass–concentration relation, carry the physics of how clusters grow.
  • Halos that form earlier are more concentrated; at fixed mass, c scatters with accretion history (Bullock+01, Wechsler+02, Neto+07).

Δm = m2 − m1, BCG vs. brightest satellite. Large gaps: satellites merged long ago (Jones+03). At fixed richness, larger gap → more massive (Hearin+13).

Vitorelli+18: stacks split by Δm. Blue: larger gap, red: smaller gap; lines are published c–M relations.
log10 c = log10 c0 + αcm log10(M/Mpiv) + βcm log10[(1+z)/(1+zpiv)] + γcm Δm

Is γcm > 0, as the fossil-group picture suggests?

~1:30 Pivot away from cluster cosmology. Concentration as a formation clock; magnitude gap as a proxy for relaxed, early-assembled systems; our 2018 stacks hinted at a shift. Everything in the paper is built to test one number: γ_cm.
04Three analyses of the same data

Same data, three analyses: fit stacks twice, fit stacks once, or do not stack at all.

Two-step stacking
the standard route
  1. Stack clusters in bins of z, λ (and Δm)
  2. Fit one NFW (M, c) to each stack
  3. Regress M, c on the stacks' mean observables
Mass of a stacked profile ≠ mean mass of its members. Biased slopes (3–6 SE in mocks) and the loosest constraints.
Forward-modelled stacking
the paper's middle path
  1. Stack clusters, exactly as before
  2. Model every member inside each stack
    ΔΣs = Σ Kc ΔΣc(θ) / Σ Kc
  3. Fit all 9 parameters θ to all stacks at once
Unbiased in mocks, but needs binning choices and stacks of ≥ 50 clusters.
Joint fit
no stacking
  1. Keep each cluster's own ΔΣc(R)
  2. Model it from its own λ, z, Δm
  3. Sum the log-likelihoods
    ℓ(θ) = Σi ℓi(θ)
Most precise; no binning, every cluster used, open to per-cluster extensions.

Forward-modelled stacking and the joint fit share model, priors and sampler: they differ only in whether the data are stacked before the likelihood.

~1:15 Walk the three columns left to right. The key design choice: the middle and right columns have exactly the same parameters, so any difference is the stacking itself.

~1:15 Click through: (1) richness gives a mass through the mass–richness relation; (2) mass and Δm give a concentration, and γ_cm sets how the pivot moves with Δm; (3) that fixes a ΔΣ(R) profile for each cluster, compared with its own data; (4) sum the log-likelihoods — nautilus only ever proposes the 9 parameters.
06Simulated clusters & lensing

Mock populations with triaxial haloes and miscentering, at DES Y3 and LSST depth.

  • Redshift z ~ U[0.1, 0.6]; mass from the Tinker+08 halo mass function, 1014–1015 M☉
  • Galaxies: central + Poisson satellites from the Zheng+07 HOD → magnitude gap Δm = m2 − m1
  • Concentration: Dutton & Macciò 14, plus γcm(Δm − 0.9); injected γcm = n/36 mag−1, n = 0…6
  • Richness by inverting M(λ) (McClintock+19 values); keep λ > 25, Δm > 0
  • Triaxial NFW haloes with random axis ratios and orientation; 36% miscentered (Rayleigh, σoff = 0.47 Mpc)
  • Sources: σe = 0.27, Smail-type n(z); 6.7 (DES-like) or 30 (LSST-like) galaxies/arcmin2
One DES-like population: gap distribution vs. real WaZP; c200 vs. mass and vs. Δm.
Triaxiality: one halo, its axes and line of sight, and the projected convergence κ
Miscentering: offsets and sky positions

~1:00 The goal is not full realism; it is to ask whether γ_cm can be recovered from plausible data. Triaxiality and miscentering are included because they are the main ways a spherical, centred model can go wrong. No cluster clustering, no selection effects (future work).
07Inference

Nine parameters, one nested-sampling run: the joint likelihood is a sum over clusters.

  • nautilus nested sampling (Lange+23)
  • 9 free parameters, same priors for joint and stacked fits
  • Posteriors to an effective sample size of 3000
  • Priors weakly informative; fmis, σoff flat

Per cluster i, residual r = data − model:

Mocks (shape-noise covariance)
ℓi = −½[ ln|Ci| + rTCi−1r ]
Real data (bootstrap, few sources per bin)
ℓi = −Σk (nik/2) ln[ 1 + rik2 / ((nik−1) sik2) ]

Sellentin–Heavens: a Student-t per bin that down-weights sparse bins.

ℓ = −½ Σs rsT Ĉs−1 rs
  • Covariance by bootstrap over member clusters (500), Hartlap-corrected
  • Model: lensing-weighted mean of the members' profiles
  • 33 stacks, each ≥ 50 clusters

Cluster bootstrap: refit 50 resamples of the cluster sample; quote the median and 16–84% range of the 50 posterior medians. It counts shape noise and sample variance once, not twice.

~1:00 Keep this short. The three things to say: nautilus; the joint likelihood is just a sum; with few sources per bin we use a Student-t (Sellentin–Heavens). Error bars come from a cluster bootstrap so they include sample variance.

The two-step analysis is also biased by 3–6 standard errors in several mass–concentration and mass–richness parameters: its first step returns masses 0.03–0.04 dex below the members' mean.

~1:30 Left: both methods unbiased in γ_cm, error bars calibrated. Right: the joint fit is the most precise — a modest 1.2–1.3× over forward-modelled stacking, a lot more over the standard two-step. Data density matters more than method: LSST-like is 5–6× tighter than DES-like.

10Results on real data

Both fits find a positive gap coupling: γcm = 0.057 (joint) vs. 0.101 mag−1 (stacked), only 1.2σ apart.

~1:15 γ_cm is positive in the fossil-group direction in both methods, at 0.057 and 0.101 per mag. Joint errors are smaller. At this point it looks like a result — the next two slides are about how far to trust it.
11The flat c–M relation

The flat mass–concentration slope is exactly what Diemer & Joyce (2019) predicts for this mass range.

Diemer & Joyce (2019) at z=0.35 is not a power law: it bottoms out near 1014.7 M☉ (top). The sample's weight sits at and beyond the minimum (bottom).
γcm with a Diemer 19 baseline instead of a free power law: 0.055 vs. 0.057.
0.03 +0.05 −0.09
αcm, joint
0.04 ± 0.09
αcm, stacked
−0.01 to 0.00
power-law slope of Diemer 19 over the sample's masses

A flat αcm is expected, not a failure. And γcm does not hinge on assuming a power law for c(M): swapping in the Diemer 19 curve leaves it at 0.055+0.017−0.015.

~1:15 Someone will ask why α_cm is zero. Answer: the Diemer & Joyce relation has an upturn; over this sample's masses a power-law slope is ~0 however you weight it. Then the check: replace the power law with their curve plus γ_cm Δm — γ_cm does not move.
12Mass at fixed richness

Let mass depend on the gap at fixed richness, and the concentration coupling nearly vanishes in both methods.

log10 M200 = log10 M0 + αMλ log10(λ/λpiv) + βMλ log10[…] + δMλ Δm
Left: 68/95% regions, δMλ free. Right: marginal γcm, δMλ = 0 (solid) vs. free (dashed).

Large-gap stacks lie 14 ± 3% above the joint prediction beyond 1 Mpc (7 ± 3% and 10 ± 3% for low and mid gaps): an amplitude excess the old model can only absorb in γcm.

  • Both prefer δMλ > 0: 0.035 (joint), 0.043 (stacked) dex mag−1. The methods differ by 0.3σ in δMλ.
  • Joint γcm = 0.007 is consistent with zero; stacked is 2σ away: neither is a detection.
  • Assembly bias or projection can both give δMλ > 0; these data cannot tell them apart.
~1:30 The key slide. Amplitude and concentration are degenerate at this S/N: a mass difference between gap bins gets absorbed in γ_cm if mass cannot depend on the gap. Free δ_Mλ and both couplings drop: 0.101→0.065 stacked, 0.057→0.007 joint. The coupling does not survive a modest extension of the model. Honest caveat: the methods still differ by 1.2σ in γ_cm; on the joint fit's radial range the stacked value is 0.048±0.047.
13Outlook

What's next

  • Real data only: WaZP vs. redMaPPer, and further concentration-related observables
  • Simulations only: a fully Bayesian hierarchical model of the scaling relations and the selection
  • Inject a gap-dependent mass (δMλ) to test the mechanism
  • Intrinsic scatter and richness selection
  • Cluster-finder selection, orientation bias, projection
  • Uncertainties on redshifts and Δm
  • Covariance beyond shape noise; overlapping apertures (92% of clusters share part of theirs)
  • Scaling relations in a per-cluster Bayesian framework, not pre-averaged summaries
  • Make the causal structure of richness, gap, mass and concentration explicit, to ask questions about formation history
